newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel passes welfare immigrant plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel passes welfare immigrant plan.

text.p: A bitterly divided House panel on Thursday moved to restore some federal benefits to legal immigrants affected by a new welfare law, as Democrats accused Republicans of violating a budget deal with the White House.

A House Ways and Means subcommittee, by a party-line vote of 8-3, approved a bill continuing federal disability aid to hundreds of thousands of legal immigrants who were scheduled to be cut off this summer under the welfare law.
Democrats claimed the Republican plan would cover far fewer immigrants than the original budget deal painstakingly worked out between Congress and the White House.
They also objected to a provision overturning a Clinton administration plan to apply minimum wage laws to welfare recipients enrolled in workfare programs.

Republicans argued that even though the budget would have allowed immigrants to qualify for benefits in the future if they became disabled, it cut off aid to too many elderly, poor immigrants already on the rolls.
Republicans, who wrote the welfare bill ending nearly all federal aid to legal immigrants, argued with the Clinton administration, which signed it into law, about which party was more compassionate.

"You're going to have suicides; you're going to have terrible, terrible problems," said Florida Republican Rep. Clay Shaw. "I'm going to stick with this position come hell or high water ... What the administration is arguing is cruel."
Michigan Democratic Rep. Sander Levin, who tried unsuccessfully to restore the budget deal, said the Republican bill covered 125,000 fewer immigrants over the next decade.
"Don't turn your back on these legal immigrants ... I just want you to pull back," Levin said.
The White House said in a letter that the bill violated the budget and did not protect the most vulnerable immigrants.
A landmark welfare law signed last year ends federal benefits to most legal immigrants this summer. Clinton won major concessions in the budget agreement to "fix" the law.

Under the budget plan, legal immigrants who were in the United States by Aug. 22, 1996, and were either on the rolls because of disability or became disabled in the future could receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and Medicaid.

Immigrants receiving SSI benefits because they were elderly and impoverished, rather than disabled, would have been cut off. Estimates were that about 20 percent of 700,000 immmigrants receiving SSI would lose aid.

Under the Republican plan all legal immigrants -- including the elderly poor -- receiving SSI on Aug. 22, 1996, could continue to get aid. Legal immigrants in the country on that date, but not on the rolls, would not be eligible for assistance even if they became disabled in the future.

Facing White House criticism, Shaw dropped on Thursday a proposal to deny benefits to immigrants who had official sponsors with incomes above 150 percent of poverty, about $25,000 for a family of four. The White House said that plan would deny aid to about 100,000 disabled immigrants.
But Shaw could not hold the votes of his party and Republicans adopted a modified proposal denying benefits to immigrants whose sponsors had an income of $40,000 or more.
"Have we come to a point in our country where nobody has an obligation to help anyone in their family or their community?" asked Louisiana Republican Jim McCrery, who sponsored the amendment.
Democrats were rebuffed in efforts to delete a provision exempting public and non-profit jobs from minimum wage laws.

Under the bill, states could count Food Stamps, cash benefits, child care, housing and medical aid when calculating hourly wages. Some governors have complained that if they paid minimum wage, they could not meet welfare work requirements. Democrats said welfare recipients would lose workplace protections and not receive fair value for their work.
Republicans dropped a plan to require immigrants to sign a pledge acknowledging that if they become a public charge, it would be grounds for deportation.
